title: Warn on pull requests targeting wrong branch
head: 609a4f40b0f8
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: publishable pending outer-assistant freshness and posting authorization

leads.summary: Backfill treats active maintenance-branch and hardware-branch PRs as wrong-base mistakes
leads.consequence: A backfill after merge will notify intentionally targeted release/dev/rc/dragon PRs that are still open to re-open against quattro, although those changes specifically belong on another branch. The current live open-PR search returns 105 PRs with base != quattro; confirmed examples include #13902 and #13848 (v4-0-4 backports), #9071 (dev), #9073 (rc), #8952 (v4-0-2), #8042 (v4-0-1), and #13820 (dragon board support). New PRs to these branches will receive the same false warning on open/reopen. Define which bases are actually erroneous, or exempt explicitly intentional maintenance branches before bulk posting.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Finding 1, reproduced); corroboration

leads.summary: Reopening an already warned PR unconditionally posts another warning
leads.consequence: The opened/reopened path never calls listComments or checks the marker. Each close/reopen cycle on a non-quattro PR posts an additional identical bot comment and notification, regardless of a prior opened/backfill warning. Check for the bot marker in this path too (or use another idempotency mechanism).
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Finding 4, reproduced); corroboration

leads.summary: Two overlapping manual backfills can both pass the marker check and post duplicates
leads.consequence: There is no workflow concurrency group or atomic claim. Two manually started runs that read an as-yet-unwarned PR before either writes each post one bot comment. A backfill racing the opened event can do the same. Serialize runs and make the event path idempotent; avoid cancelling a run mid-backfill without resuming it.
leads.triage: requires two concurrent manual dispatches; low value; dropped

leads.summary: The write-capable pull_request_target workflow executes a mutable v7 action tag
leads.consequence: Both jobs resolve actions/github-script@v7 at execution time. A tag move or compromised action release changes the code executed with pull-requests:write even when the repository workflow is unchanged, including for fork PR events. The v7 tag resolved to commit f28e40c7f34bde8b3046d885e986cb6290c5673b during this review. Pin to an audited full SHA; the related CI PR #10181 already SHA-pins checkout, but its separate workflow does not secure this one.
leads.triage: already in Opus optional notes; corroboration

leads.summary: A 500-comment backfill exceeds the standard GITHUB_TOKEN primary REST limit even from an empty hourly bucket
leads.consequence: The standard GITHUB_TOKEN allowance is 1,000 REST calls per hour per repository (15,000 for GitHub Enterprise Cloud accounts). A run with 500 unmarked wrong-base PRs in today's 2,851-open-PR repository needs at least 29 pull-list pages + 500 issue-comment-list reads + 500 create-comment writes = 1,029 API requests in about 9 minutes. Thus on the standard 1,000-call tier it necessarily hits a 403/429 before posting all 500, with no retry/backoff. Even an Enterprise account shares secondary content-creation limits of generally 500 requests/hour. Lower the run cap or budget calls against the observed rate headers, pause/resume after reset, and avoid listing unaffected/commented PRs where possible. Current 105 non-quattro PRs are below this bound; this is a future/full-cap failure, and the organization's enterprise billing tier was not observable.
leads.triage: factual JS behaviour, adjacent to Opus Finding 3; not published separately

leads.summary: Malformed manual limit silently becomes 500 or a truncated prefix
leads.consequence: The input is type:string, and parseInt('2garbage',10) is 2; parseInt('foo',10) is NaN and requestedLimit || 500 becomes 500. A malformed user-supplied cap thus silently authorizes the full 500-comment run instead of failing validation. Require a fully decimal integer within the documented 1..500 range, or explicitly tell the caller when falling back.
leads.triage: source-only hypothesis, no failing PR identified; dropped

leads.summary: One recurring PR-specific API failure prevents backfill from reaching every later PR
leads.consequence: If listComments or createComment persistently rejects for a particular PR (e.g. documented 403/404/410 responses), the uncaught rejection fails the whole job before it reaches the later pull requests. Re-running lists the same open PRs in the same created-desc order and stops at the same one again. Distinguish per-PR failures that may be skipped and reported from global auth/rate-limit failures that should stop and be retried according to Retry-After; no network run was performed.

limits: Enterprise Cloud organization billing status for omacom was not exposed by gh api orgs/omacom (public plan:null); H7's primary-rate exhaustion is conditional on the documented standard GITHUB_TOKEN tier.

GitHub's branch-name filter says SHA-like pull_request_target heads may not trigger (docs/events.md:678), so such a PR may rely on manual backfill. No live event was fired; no actual omission claimed.

Only identified workflow-adjacent open PRs and intentionally targeted maintenance PRs were inspected. A broad initial title/topic search produced hundreds of unrelated PRs, so this is not a complete diff-by-diff review of the repository's thousands of open PRs.

flags.claim: Suggested change: `Number.isNaN(n) ? 500 : Math.min(Math.max(n, 0), 500)`, or a `type: number` input.
flags.disposition: real error: dropped 'or a type: number input'

flags.disposition: real error: job-level if now includes event_name guard; note later removed to keep 3 optional notes

flags.claim: Suggested change: document the needed event policy, or run the backfill on a `schedule`.
flags.disposition: real error: schedule alternative moved to Details with wider job if and inputs?.limit

flags.claim: Suggested change: warn only for retired bases (e.g. `branches: [dev]` plus the same list in the backfill).
flags.disposition: real error: suggestion now 'bases the maintainers retire', branches list under pull_request_target; dev example removed

flags.claim: Impact: they and future backports get told to reopen against `quattro`.
flags.disposition: real error: quote 'open it against quattro' and backfill/warn-job split

flags.claim: Impact: duplicate warnings on reopened wrong-base PRs.
flags.disposition: nitpick, trivial fix applied: 'an already-warned PR that is reopened'

issues.requirement: Readable comments (2026-09-28): visible text (everything outside <details> blocks, including heading and footer) must be at most 1,500 characters.
issues.excerpt: Measured visible length (characters outside <details> blocks, including heading and footer): 4618. Budget: 1,500.
issues.correction: Reduce the measured visible length to 1,500 characters or less. Each Reproducer block nests a `<details><summary>repro.js</summary>` block, and the same repro.js appears three times. If the measurement pairs the outer `<details>` with the inner `</details>`, the reproducer commands, outputs and `gh api` data are counted as visible. Include repro.js once, without nesting; for example, put it in the first Reproducer block and have the other two refer to it by mode. Remove the other nested `<details>` so each collapsed block has a single open and close tag. If the re-measured visible text still exceeds 1,500, move the `pull_request_target` finding into the collapsed `More findings` block with its heading, Impact and Suggested change.

retro:
# Retro: #11747

- Worked: parallel Opus + Sol hunt; the hunter corroborated both main Opus findings independently (intentional bases, reopen duplicate) and added the malformed-limit lead.
- Self-check caught three incomplete suggestions carried over from the reviewer's own report (`type: number` does not fix limit 0; job-level `if` lacked the event_name guard; schedule alternative needs a wider job `if` and optional `inputs`) and one lost qualifier (dev retirement is a maintainer call). Suggestions deserve the same fact check as findings.
- Friction: the 1,500 visible budget with two medium findings plus the fixed AI-process line required several trim passes; lesser findings went into a collapsed More findings block.
- The three reproducers share one repro.js pasted three times (verbatim rule); the comment is ~21 KB. Acceptable, but a shared-script reproducer format could shorten comments.
- No process deviations.
